rules.approval_rationale: Separates artifact existence from governed evidentiary admission.
counterexamples: The agent generated a report, so it was automatically admitted as proof.
rules.description: Admitted claims require a named admission decision, authority record, and claim scope.
may_say: A named decision admitted the specified claim or artifact within scope.
must_never_claim: Submission, generation, or presence equals admission
must_refuse: Claims that an actor report or artifact was automatically admitted
must_say: Admission decision, authority record, and claim scope
positive_examples: The named authority decision admitted the artifact for the declared claim.

rules.approval_rationale: Keeps inspection language tied to an observable method and bounded object.
counterexamples: The system was inspected, so all components are secure.
rules.description: Inspected claims require a named artifact, inspection method, and claim scope.
may_infer: Findings directly produced by the named inspection
may_say: The named artifact was inspected through the declared method.
must_refuse: Generic inspected claims with no method or scope
must_say: Artifact, inspection method, and claim scope
positive_examples: The named manifest was inspected with the declared offline verification procedure.

templates.body: A fit check is a non-secret first step to determine whether the work is bounded enough for a WitnessOps proof package. It does not commit to a final package or start a proof run. Scope, fee, timing, and evidence handling are agreed before any work begins. Request a fit check at /review/request.
counterexamples: submitting raw evidence
demanding a final package assignment
synthetic_positive_cases: asking what belongs in first contact
asking whether one bounded action may fit

templates.body: A proof packet is a bounded set of materials linking the agreed scope to evidence references, receipts where produced, named limits, and a path for inspection or challenge. It supports the named action and boundary only. It does not establish total system truth, complete security, or conclusions beyond the declared scope.
counterexamples: total-system proof
public customer-evidence upload

templates.body: A receipt records a bounded issuance or action claim and relates that claim to declared evidence or verification layers. It supports only the claim and boundary it names. A receipt does not establish complete source-system truth, perfect judgment, total security, or conclusions outside its declared scope.
counterexamples: complete environment truth
launch-package selection

templates.body: A verification path names the artifact, verifier, proof path, and claim scope. Any verdict is limited to the submitted input, verification mode, and checks that were actually performed; it is not a generic assurance. The public guide can explain that process, but it cannot inspect or verify a private system.
counterexamples: private-system verdict
compliance guarantee

templates.body: A launch-readiness question may fit Workflow M or a Launch Readiness Review, but that guidance is provisional. The work must have a named system and an authorized, read-only boundary where applicable; it is not compliance certification. Scope, fee, timing, and evidence handling are agreed before work starts. Begin with a non-secret fit check at /review/request.
counterexamples: compliance certification
security disclosure

templates.body: A vendor change may fit Workflow S, Workflow M, or a bounded re-run. “Vendor Action Proof Capsule” describes a request shape, not a standalone SKU: one named action or system boundary with explicit limits. Final fit depends on scope, and scope, fee, timing, and evidence handling are agreed before work starts. Use /review/request for a non-secret fit check.
counterexamples: vendor-wide security guarantee
receipt definition

templates.body: A bounded AI-agent action may fit Workflow S. “AI-Agent Action Receipt” describes a request shape for one named agent action or change lane; an agent’s own report is not automatically admitted as proof. Final fit depends on scope, and scope, fee, timing, and evidence handling are agreed before work starts. Use /review/request for a non-secret fit check.
counterexamples: complete AI-governance certification
private model-host disclosure

templates.body: An incident-readiness question may fit Workflow L or an Incident Readiness Pack, with known facts kept separate from inference and unresolved gaps. This is not hack-back guidance or emergency response, and logs or screenshots should not be sent as a first step. Final fit depends on scope; scope, fee, timing, and evidence handling are agreed before work starts. Begin with a non-secret fit check at /review/request.
counterexamples: hack-back
immediate raw-log intake

templates.body: An access-authority question may fit Workflow S or M. The bounded review focuses on who approved access, what was allowed, what occurred, and where authority stopped; “Authority Map Sprint” is a request shape, not a standalone commitment. It does not authorize bypasses or private-record disclosure. Start with a non-secret fit check at /review/request. Scope, fee, timing, and evidence handling are agreed before work starts.
counterexamples: approval bypass
private-record disclosure
superseded_representations: Scope, fee, timing, and evidence handling are agreed before work starts through /review/request.

templates.body: Offline inspection may fit Workflow S, a Local Server Audit, or a Pilot entry. “Offline Verification Kit” describes a request shape using named artifacts, manifests, sidecars, verifier instructions, and explicit limits. Its strength is bounded by the included artifacts and verifier contract. Final fit, scope, fee, timing, and evidence handling are agreed through a non-secret fit check at /review/request.
counterexamples: whole-runtime proof
private-key submission

templates.body: WitnessOps workspace access is private preview only and is separate from a proof run. There is no public signup, checkout, or self-service provisioning path. Workspace access does not by itself verify activity, and it does not imply a publicly available SaaS, marketplace, app, or OffSec portal.
counterexamples: package fit
receipt verification

templates.body: Use the approved public responsible-disclosure path and keep the first report non-secret and redacted. Do not include credentials, keys, customer data, raw logs, screenshots, private infrastructure details, or exploit instructions. Reporting does not authorize further testing, and acknowledgment does not mean triage or remediation is complete.
counterexamples: exploit procedure
raw credential submission

templates.body: Public WitnessOps support covers product help, access help, and verifier questions. It is not an emergency or 24/7 incident-response service, and it cannot expose private records or infrastructure. Use the approved public support route for general assistance.
counterexamples: emergency response
private-record access

templates.body: Do not paste that here. Start with a non-secret fit check. WitnessOps agrees scope and evidence handling before receiving customer evidence. This public guide does not accept raw evidence.
